p|panel|qv_ext_lee_ia: It can read what you see and type on any website, including your conversations with an AI.

p|panel|qv_ext_quitar_edge: If you don't recognize it, remove it in Edge: edge://extensions › Remove.
p|panel|qv_ext_quitar_brave: If you don't recognize it, remove it in Brave: brave://extensions › Remove.
p|panel|qv_ext_quitar_firefox: If you don't recognize it, remove it in Firefox: about:addons › ··· › Remove.

p|panel|qv_ext_ninguna: No extensions installed in Chrome, Edge, Brave or Firefox.
p|panel|qv_ext_sin_cuentas: Could not read the account folders on this computer.
p|panel|qv_aj_publicidad_que: Lets apps show you personalized ads using an ID that follows you from one app to the next.
p|panel|qv_aj_experiencias_que: Microsoft uses your diagnostic data to show you personalized tips, ads and recommendations.
p|panel|qv_aj_diagnostico_que: Sends Microsoft more detail about how you use Windows and your apps, including the websites you visit. When off, only the required data is sent. Applies to the whole computer.
p|panel|qv_aj_anuncios_apple_que: Apple uses information about you to choose the ads in the App Store, Apple News and Stocks. Turn it off in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Apple Advertising.
p|panel|qv_aj_cuentas: Applies to the {n} accounts on this computer.
p|panel|qv_aj_otro: This check is not available on this computer.
p|panel|qv_ia_titulo: Your AI services and who they talk to
p|panel|qv_ia_ext: {n} extensions can read your AI chats
p|panel|qv_ia_ext_uno: 1 extension can read your AI chats
p|panel|qv_ia_vacio: This computer did not use any known AI service in this period.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_chatgpt: To keep your chats out of training: Settings › Data controls › turn off “Improve the model for everyone”. The Free and Go plans may show ads; OpenAI says it does not sell conversations.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_claude: To keep your chats out of training: Settings › Privacy › turn off “Help improve Claude”.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_gemini: To keep your chats out of training: in Gemini Apps Activity (myactivity.google.com/product/gemini), turn off “Keep Activity”.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_copilot: To keep your chats out of training: Settings › Privacy › turn off “Model training on text” and “Model training on voice”.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_grok: To keep your chats out of training: Settings › Data Controls › turn off “Improve the Model”.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_perplexity: To keep your chats out of training: Settings › Preferences › turn off “AI data retention”.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_mistral: To keep your chats out of training: in Le Chat, Settings › Privacy, turn off the use of your data for training.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_meta: Meta AI has no general switch to keep your chats out of training; in the EU and the UK you can object through the form in Meta's Privacy Center.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_deepseek: Its privacy policy says it may use what you type to improve its models and that the data is stored in China. Don't share personal data unless Settings offers a way to turn this off.
p|panel|qv_ia_guia_otra: Look in this service's privacy settings for an option about using your chats to train or improve its models, and turn it off.
p|panel|qv_fab_vacio: No program signed by the computer's manufacturer (HP, Dell, Lenovo, ASUS…) connected in this period.
p|panel|qv_fab_no_windows: Only Windows says which program made each query: on this system the manufacturer's programs cannot be told apart.
p|panel|qv_av_vacio: Windows reports no antivirus installed other than Microsoft Defender.
p|panel|qv_av_no_leido: This check is not available on this computer.
p|panel|qv_tv_titulo: TVs at home that report what you watch
p|panel|qv_tv_sin_hogar: To see the TVs at home, turn on Home Mode.
p|panel|qv_tv_que: This is automatic content recognition (ACR): the TV recognizes what is on screen and reports it. Turn it off in the TV's privacy settings.
p|panel|qv_tv_vacio: No device at home called a known content recognition service.
p|panel|qv_sig_dice: A data broker gathers what people do on their devices and sells it or combines it with other sources.
p|panel|qv_sig_mas: Here you see who on this computer talks to one of those companies. It is not an alarm: you decide whether to allow it, block it or turn it off.
p|panel|qv_limites: What GUARDIANA sees and what it doesn't
p|panel|qv_lim_ve: It sees who each program talks to, which extensions are installed and this computer's settings.
p|panel|qv_lim_no: It does not see what a company does with the data once it has it, or what happens inside your cloud accounts.
p|panel|qv_lim_nombres: It sees destination names, never the content: it decrypts nothing.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-avast-2024: The FTC fined Avast $16.5 million and banned it from selling browsing data for advertising: it sold that data through Jumpshot, collected by its antivirus and browser extensions.
p|panel|qv_caso_koi-urbanvpn-2025: Koi Security found that Urban VPN Proxy and seven other extensions (about 8 million installs on Chrome and Edge) had captured conversations with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Grok and other AIs since July 2025 and shared them with the data broker BiScience.
p|panel|qv_caso_texas-acr-2025: Texas sued Sony, Samsung, LG, Hisense and TCL for using automatic content recognition (ACR) to capture what people watch on their TVs without proper consent.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-gm-2026: The FTC finalized its order against General Motors and OnStar for selling location and driving data to LexisNexis and Verisk without consent: they may not share it with those agencies for five years.
p|panel|qv_caso_openai-anuncios-2026: OpenAI began testing ads in ChatGPT for the Free and Go plans; it says it does not sell conversations to advertisers.
p|panel|qv_caso_anthropic-entrenamiento-: Anthropic changed its consumer terms: chats on Claude Free, Pro and Max are used to train its models unless you turn that off.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-lenovo-2017: Lenovo settled with the FTC over VisualDiscovery (Superfish), ad software preinstalled on its laptops that intercepted connections, including secure ones.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-kochava-2022: The FTC sued Kochava for selling location data from hundreds of millions of phones that reveals visits to clinics, places of worship and shelters.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-xmode-2024: The FTC banned X-Mode Social (Outlogic) from selling sensitive location data.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-inmarket-2024: The FTC banned InMarket from selling or licensing precise location data.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-gravy-2024: The FTC took action against Gravy Analytics and its subsidiary Venntel for selling sensitive location data without consent.
p|panel|qv_caso_ftc-mobilewalla-2024: The FTC took action against Mobilewalla for collecting and selling sensitive location data, including data taken from ad auctions.
p|panel|qv_caso_listas-tv: Public blocklists for TVs (PiHoleBlocklist, SmartTV list) identify these names as tracking and content recognition.
p|panel|au_frase: Check that the installed program is the published one, every connection GUARDIANA makes and everything it keeps on your disk.
p|panel|au_inst_titulo: The installed program is the published one
p|panel|au_inst_coincide: Every file of the installed program has the same SHA-256 hash as the version published in the public record.
p|panel|au_inst_no_coincide: A file of the installed program is not in the public record, or the record was not found on this computer.
p|panel|au_reg_sin_archivo_que: Download ledger.jsonl from GUARDIANA's website into the program folder and audit again.
p|panel|au_reg_zip_que: On a Mac, the public record holds the hash of the .zip you downloaded, not of the program inside it: compare that hash with the downloaded file.
p|panel|au_firma_no_signature_file: No signature file next to the program
p|panel|au_firma_dev_key: Development build: no signature to check
p|panel|au_rekor: See the entry in the Rekor public log
p|panel|au_con_vacio: GUARDIANA has made no connections of its own on this computer.
p|panel|au_con_mas: And {n} older connections in the full report.
p|panel|au_con_mas_uno: And 1 older connection in the full report.
p|panel|au_con_nota: Names only, never addresses. Each connection is written down when it is made: license, updates, lists and calls.
p|panel|au_disco_titulo: What it keeps on your disk
p|panel|au_ip_locales: {n} local addresses (this computer or devices on your home network), never internet ones.
p|panel|au_ip_locales_uno: 1 local address (this computer or a device on your home network), never an internet one.
p|panel|au_contenido: It keeps destination names and times, never the content of what you send or receive.
p|panel|au_sig_dice: You don't have to take GUARDIANA's word for it: you can audit it yourself, with what is on your own computer.
p|panel|au_sig_mas: Every check runs here and sends nothing. The report comes with a seal anyone can recompute.
p|panel|au_trabajando: Auditing: computing hashes, reading records and tables…
p|panel|au_veredicto_bien: Checked: published program, chain intact and no internet addresses stored
p|panel|au_veredicto_revisar: Something to review: see the section marked in amber
p|panel|au_sellado_que: Sealed, not signed: the report's SHA-256 hash proves nobody changed it afterward. This computer holds no private key to sign it. A seal or a signature checks that the report and the program are intact, not that there is no activity GUARDIANA could not observe.
p|panel|au_cadena_cabeza: Latest link of the log's chain:
p|panel|borrar_lead: Deletes the ledger, the devices, the rules, the declared scopes, the gaps without watching, the changes made by GUARDIANA and this record. It cannot be undone.
p|panel|borrar_confirmar: This deletes everything and cannot be undone. Type DELETE to confirm:
p|panel|clave_dev: development key, not the release key
p|panel|dns_aplicado_falta: pointed at GUARDIANA, except a connection that is asking another DNS right now (a new network or adapter, or GUARDIANA set aside because the network was not answering). It points it back by itself as soon as it can, usually within a minute.
p|panel|estado_limite: Home Mode is not part of version 1.0 on a Mac: GUARDIANA does not manage the macOS firewall and we have not tested it there the way we did on Windows, so we do not vouch for it yet; the site says the same. Changing the system DNS and the service that starts by itself do work on all three.
p|panel|hogar_lead: Turns this PC into the DNS guardian of the home Wi‑Fi: phones, TV and everything that uses the Wi‑Fi, without installing anything on them.
p|panel|hogar_estado_on: Home Mode on since {fecha}. GUARDIANA listens on the IP {ip} of your local network.
p|panel|hogar_estado_fuera: Home Mode is on, but paused: this computer is not on the network where you switched it on, and away from home it opens no port toward the network. It comes back by itself when you are home. If you moved or changed routers, switch it off and on again here.
p|panel|hogar_estado_off: Home Mode off. GUARDIANA listens only on this PC; no port open toward the network.
p|panel|hogar_estado_aparcado: Home Mode set aside: the trial or the subscription ended. Your router still sends the home’s queries here, so GUARDIANA only passes them on, without looking at them or writing them down. It comes back on by itself once you activate your key.
p|panel|hogar_desactivar_relevo: Switch off completely (I put the router’s DNS back)
p|panel|hogar_que_pasa: When turned on, GUARDIANA opens ports only on your local network, never toward the internet: the DNS (53), this panel (7443) and the checker page (80). It is recorded in the ledger. Turning it off closes them. The change takes under a minute; if the Wi‑Fi connects later or changes address, GUARDIANA notices by itself.
p|panel|hogar_ip_dinamica: Notice: the IP {ip} of this PC is assigned by the router and may change. If it changes, the phones will lose their DNS. Reserve this IP for this PC in the router (“DHCP reservation”, usually under Local network › DHCP) or set a fixed IP.
p|panel|hogar_ip_fija: The IP {ip} of this PC looks fixed. Good.
p|panel|hogar_ip_desconocida: Could not tell whether the IP {ip} is fixed or assigned by the router. If it changes, the phones will lose their DNS: better reserve it in the router.
p|panel|hogar_primero: To connect a phone, first turn Home Mode on with the button above. Once it is on, the steps appear here, with the exact address to type on the phone.
p|panel|hogar_qr_lead: Scan this code with the phone: it opens the step-by-step guide on it, and the same page tells it whether it already goes through GUARDIANA.
p|panel|hogar_url: Or type in the phone’s browser:
p|panel|hogar_router_texto: In the router, under the DHCP settings, set the IP {ip} as the DNS server. Every device on the Wi‑Fi is covered without touching them. If the provider’s router does not allow it, use the per-phone guide.
p|panel|hogar_iphone_pasos: Settings › Wi‑Fi › tap the (i) of your network › Configure DNS › Manual › delete the servers already there (red circle) › Add Server › type {ip} › Save.
p|panel|hogar_android_pasos: Settings › Wi‑Fi › long-press your network › Modify › Advanced options › IP settings: Static › DNS 1: {ip}. Many Android phones also require a fixed IP for the phone: pick a free one on your network (for example the one it already has) and leave the rest as it is.
p|panel|hogar_comprobar_texto: On the phone, open http://comprobar.guardiana.hogar and, if the page “This device already goes through GUARDIANA” loads, it is done. Only GUARDIANA resolves that name.
p|panel|hogar_prueba: Home Mode has no limit of its own: it goes with the license, like everything else. What matters is that this PC is on.
p|panel|hogar_limite: Only on the home Wi‑Fi. On mobile data or away from home, the phone does not go through GUARDIANA. GUARDIANA sees service names, not which app asked for them. The phone’s page travels over your Wi‑Fi unencrypted: anyone with the network password could see it. If this PC shuts down or sleeps, phones pointing only at it are left without DNS until it comes back.
p|panel|hogar_no_admin: Opening the ports and the firewall rule requires running GUARDIANA as administrator.
p|panel|hogar_firewall_manual: On this system the firewall rule is added by hand, and only if you have one running: let in, from your local network, ports 53 (udp and tcp), 7443/tcp (the phones’ panel) and 80/tcp (the checker page). With ufw: sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 53 && sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 7443 proto tcp && sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 80 proto tcp (if your network starts with 10., use 10.0.0.0/8 instead of 192.168.0.0/16). With firewalld, in your Wi‑Fi’s zone (see it with “firewall-cmd --get-active-zones”; here, home): sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=home --add-service=dns --add-port=7443/tcp --add-port=80/tcp && sudo firewall-cmd --reload.
